body_long:
Nobu is entering the Kingdom of Bahrain. On 12 November 2026, Nobu Hospitality announced a partnership with Infracorp to develop a new Nobu destination at Marina Bay, on Reef Island, along the waterfront in Manama.

## Hotel, restaurant and residences

The project brings together a Nobu hotel, a signature Nobu restaurant and Nobu-branded residences. It spans around 51,000 square metres of gross floor area and is expected to be developed over three years. The number of rooms and residences is to be confirmed.

According to the release, the destination will combine Japanese-inspired design, signature cuisine and personalised service with the character of its waterfront setting.

## The signing

The agreement was signed at Infracorp's headquarters in Manama by Trevor Horwell, Chief Executive Officer of Nobu Hospitality, and Talal Al Mahroos, Chief Executive Officer of Infracorp, in the presence of Fatima bint Jaffar Al Sairaifi, Minister of Tourism and Chairperson of the Bahrain Tourism and Exhibitions Authority. Struan McKenzie, COO of Nobu Hospitality, and Hisham Alrayes, Chairman of Infracorp, also attended, and the Bahrain Economic Development Board supported the talks.

"We believe Bahrain has tremendous potential," said Trevor Horwell. For Infracorp, Nobu's reputation makes it "a natural fit for Marina Bay".

## A dense Gulf pipeline

Bahrain joins a long list of Nobu projects in the region. The brand lists hotels coming soon in Abu Dhabi, Al Khobar, Muscat and Al Marjan Island, with residences also planned in Kuwait.

## The signal

In the Gulf, the restaurant name now opens the door. Nobu enters a new country with its table, then builds the hotel and the homes around it. For developers, a famous dining brand is the fastest way to give a new waterfront district an address people already know.
